C0.quote: designing voting rules that take as input the ordinal preferences
C0.note: Single-winner voting rules evaluated by distortion.

C1.quote: simultaneously achieve near-optimal distortion guarantees in both distortion worlds
C1.note: All main results are upper and lower bounds on metric and utilitarian distortion.

C2.1.value: preference profile; preference ranking; top-t preference profile
C2.1.quote: Collectively, they form a preference profile ~σ = (σ1 , σ2 , . . . , σn )

C2.2.quote: we only have each agent’s ranking for their top-t preferences
C2.2.note: OTH: top-t prefixes of rankings (partial rankings).

C2.3.quote: We assume that the preference profile stems from underlying cardinal preferences
C2.3.note: Cardinal utilities and metric costs are held attitudes; the ranking is also described as held.

C2.4.quote: Each agent i ∈ N has a preference ranking σi ∈ L(A)
C2.4.note: The rule is applied directly to the held ranking. Cardinal utilities are separate objects, but no statement relates submitted rankings to held rankings beyond 'ask each agent to report' in the introduction. DIST was considered.

C3.2.note: No statement that agents report their true rankings.

C4.1.note: Consistency of rankings with utilities and with metrics is formally defined.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: The utilitarian distortion of distribution over alternatives p ∈ ∆(A)
C5.1.note: Results concern distortion and social welfare.

C5.2.quote: worst-case distortion of f (~σ ) on any utility profile
C5.2.note: Evaluation is against cardinal utilities or metric costs, defined separately from the input.

VOT.quote_behav: takes as input a preference profile ~σ and outputs
VOT.note: Rankings are treated as exogenous inputs.

DES.note: Authors design rules, but no designer agent is modelled.

approximately optimal welfare will be achieved with respect to all possible

C9.2.note: The claims about real deployment and achieved welfare need submitted rankings to equal held rankings; this is not stated. The utility-ranking link is stated.

C1.reason: The paper designs rules and proves distortion bounds but gives no running-time, hardness or complexity results, so AL does not apply.

C2.2.reason: Section 5's main results take top-t partial rankings as input, which is a format beyond strict full rankings and so needs OTH.

C6.VOT.reason: The codebook counts agents whose actions are fixed as present, and agents supply rankings to the rule (described as reporting in the introduction), so voters are present as non-strategic agents with implicit behaviour.
